 Tampa Bay Rays Officially Release 29-Year-Old Infielder
 Originally posted on
 Viral Sports News 
  | 
 By Simeon Kotto
  | 
 Last updated Oct 31, 2026 3:34 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 Oliver Dunn has once again reached free agency after the Tampa Bay Rays removed him from their 40-man roster during the 2026 season. 
 The left-handed hitting infielder has elected minor league free agency following an outright assignment to Triple-A Durham earlier in the fall, via MLB transaction records .
 For a player who has bounced between organizations and spent most of his career in the minors, the move marks another chapter in a familiar cycle of opportunity and reset.
 Dunn, who turns 29 in September 2027, entered the majors with the Milwaukee Brewers in 2024 after a winding path through the Yankees and Phillies systems. 
 Drafted by New York in the 11th round out of the University of Utah in 2019, he showed power and on-base skills at Double-A before a trade brought him to Milwaukee. 
 He appeared in 41 games that first season, hitting .221 with a home run and three steals, mostly in a reserve role. A more limited look in 2025 produced a .167 average over 14 games. After electing free agency that winter, he signed a minor league contract with the Chicago White Sox and reported to spring training as a non-roster invitee.
 His 2026 campaign began productively in the White Sox organization. 
 Across 41 games with Triple-A Charlotte, Dunn slashed .295/.393/.545 with nine home runs and nine steals, flashing the contact and pop that have long defined his minor league profile. 
 In mid-May, the White Sox dealt him to the Rays for left-hander Joe Rock. 
 Tampa Bay immediately selected his contract and inserted him into the major league roster while Ben Williamson recovered from injury. 
 Dunn appeared in nine games, mostly as a late-inning substitute, collecting one hit in 11 at-bats for a .091 average and a single RBI. 
 The Rays optioned him back to Durham after that brief window, then designated him for assignment in early September before outrighting him once he cleared waivers.
 Across three big-league seasons with Milwaukee and Tampa Bay, Dunn owns a .197/.253/.275 line in 157 plate appearances, with one home run, 14 RBIs and four steals. 
 He has shown the ability to handle multiple infield positions and has logged time in left field in the minors, giving clubs a flexible defensive option. His baserunning instincts remain an asset as well. 
 Those traits should help him land another minor league deal this winter, though the fact that he is out of options will make it harder for any team to carry him on a 40-man roster for long stretches without a clear everyday path.
 For Dunn the pattern is well established. Strong stretches in Triple-A continue to earn him brief looks in the majors, only for roster math and performance to return him to free agency. 
 Whether another organization views his versatility and minor league production as worth the risk will determine how much time he spends in the big leagues in 2027.
